## What you will learn?
Reproducible research requires more than shared code. It connects well-managed data, versioned analyses, computational environments, and documented results. 
Through this [course]{.content-visible unless-profile="workshop"}[workshop]{.content-visible when-profile="workshop"} you will learn to:

::::: {.home-goal}
:::: {.home-goal-list}
- **Organize** a project, and keep the raw data untouched
- **Track** every change with Git and collaborate through GitHub
- **Lock** the software version with Pixi, and ship it in containers
- **Report** results with Quarto and Jupyter - literate programming
- **Automate** the pipeline with Snakemake and Nextflow
- **Share** it with an open license and archive on Zenodo
::::

:::: {.home-goal-card}
[The goal]{.home-card-kicker}

[Create research others can reproduce and build upon]{.home-goal-title}

2. []{.bi .bi-box-seam aria-hidden="true"} Environment & workflow

:::

##  Project-based learning
Learn through a guided genomics project, then apply the skills to your own research.

::::: {.home-cards .home-cards-2}
:::: {.home-card .home-project}
[Guided genomics project]{.home-card-kicker}

### The LTEE project

Work with sequencing data from the [Long-Term Evolution Experiment (LTEE)](pages/ltee-project.qmd) to develop a version-controlled, portable, and automated variant analysis workflow.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="course"}
[More about the project ](assessment/ltee-project.qmd){.home-card-link}
:::
::::
:::: {.home-card .home-capstone}
[Apply to your own research]{.home-card-kicker}

### Your capstone project

Apply the principles and tools learned in the course to organize, document, automate, and share an analysis from your own research.

[The capstone](assessment/capstone-rubric.qmd){.home-card-link}

## What is in every lesson

:::: {.home-steps}
::: {.home-step}
[1]{.home-step-number}

### Slides: the *why*

A short slide deck that gives the background and the motivation.
:::
::: {.home-step}
[2]{.home-step-number}

### Tutorial: the *how*

Self-contained, with copy-and-paste commands, expected output, exercises and
troubleshooting.
:::
::: {.home-step}
[3]{.home-step-number}

### *Break it*

Each lesson ends by breaking something on purpose, so you see what the tool
protects you from.
:::

## Built on open material

This course began as a [mini-course at Stanford Biosciences](https://explorecourses.stanford.edu/search?q=BIOS+259&view=catalog&page=0&filter-coursestatus-Active=on&collapse=&academicYear=20232024)
([BIOS259, Winter 2024](https://github.com/asntech/bios259-w24/)), developed by Aziz Khan and taught with the help of
Alvina, Clemens and Brennan.

The material adapts and extends open lessons from [NBIS](https://nbisweden.github.io/),
[Software Carpentry](https://software-carpentry.org), [Data Carpentry](https://datacarpentry.org/) and many more. See [Sources and credits](pages/credits.qmd).
::::
:::: {.home-footer-side}
